correctness.rationale: The claim fixes \(h\ge2\), level sizes \(r_i\ge2\), integral coefficients, and the ordinal-sum convention. The proof identifies the top chain group with \(\bigotimes_i\mathbb Z[A_i]\), separates boundary components by the omitted level, and therefore identifies top homology with \(\bigotimes_i\ker\varepsilon_i\). For an arbitrary order-preserving self-map, the top-chain map is factored through partial level maps \(g_i\); nonzero action forces every indicator \(\varepsilon_i g_i\) to vanish on the augmentation kernel, which forces every level to be preserved. The remaining rank calculation is exactly \(\prod_i(s_i-1)\). The included verifier independently computes the induced top-chain maps for all self-maps of three small weak orders and agrees with every predicted rank. No finite computation is used to justify the quantified theorem.

value.rationale: Finite weak orders are a natural and broad class whose order complexes are the standard multipartite pseudospheres. The theorem turns that object-level join structure into a map-level rigidity principle: any cross-level motion annihilates top homology, while every surviving map has an exact rank determined only by level-image sizes. It also gives a closed count of all homologically nontrivial self-maps and a homological characterization of homeomorphisms. This is structural rather than a small census or parameter increment, and it simultaneously explains special complete-bipartite and all-two-point-level cases.
